To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of personalized recommender systems can have a positive impact on learning, and this effect is not limited to specific learning tasks; (ii) the effect of personalized recommendations on learning depends on the learner’s personality and on the type of recommender system, and (iii) the effect of recommender systems on learning is mediated by the perceived usefulness of the recommender system.
recommender systems have a great potential to facilitate learning, but that this potential is not automatically realized.
• Recommender systems have the potential to improve the learning experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a recommender system that supports learners in finding and selecting appropriate learning material for their learning needs.

how recommender systems can support learning in a variety of ways, both in formal learning contexts (e.g., in school or university) and in informal learning contexts (e. g., in museums or in leisure time).
the question of how the design of recommender systems can be informed by psychological theories and empirical findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current research is not yet able to provide a clear answer to the question of whether or not the use of recommender systems can be recommended as a general means to enhance learning.
recommender systems have a great potential for learning, and that they can contribute to a more effective, efficient, and enjoyable learning.
the current state of recommender systems is not yet mature enough for a transfer into the domain of education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recommender system has been successful in helping students to learn, and that the system has been successful because of the students.
we need to understand how to design recommender systems that are effective for learning, and how to understand learning with recommender systems.
recommender systems are not just for shopping, but can also be used for learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of recommender systems is not a one-to-one transfer from commercial to educational settings, but requires careful adaptations to educational contexts and to learners.
recommender systems can be a very powerful tool for learning.
recommender systems can be very helpful for learning.
